# Preparing RINEX Observations with RTKlib: 30-Second Decimation and Formatting {#sec-rtklib-prep}

::: {.callout-note}
### Purpose of this Chapter
Before submitting raw GNSS logs from your Emlid Reach RS2 to the **IBGE PPP** (Precise Point Positioning) service, you must ensure the observation file complies with geodetic standards. High-rate field recordings (e.g., 1 Hz or 5 Hz) generate massive files that exceed IBGE upload limits and cause processing timeouts. 

This chapter details how to use **RTKCONV** (the graphical conversion tool in the open-source **RTKLIB** suite) to decimate observations to the required **30-second interval**, standardize RINEX versioning, and configure header metadata.
:::

## Why Decimate Records to 30-Second Intervals?

When collecting field data with an Emlid Reach RS2, the receiver typically logs at **1 Hz (1 measurement per second)** or **5 Hz (5 measurements per second)**. While high sampling rates are necessary for kinematic drone tracking or dynamic mobile trajectories, they are detrimental to static PPP processing:

1. **Server Payload Rejection:** A 4-hour static survey logged at 5 Hz contains $72,000$ epochs, producing an uncompressed RINEX file of $150\text{ to }300\text{ MB}$. IBGE PPP web interfaces frequently reject files exceeding $10\text{ to }20\text{ MB}$ or fail during transmission.
2. **Computational Redundancy:** Static PPP relies on the geometry change of GNSS satellites orbiting the Earth over several hours. Satellites move relatively slowly across the sky; recording phase measurements every $0.2\text{ seconds}$ versus every $30\text{ seconds}$ does not improve the final position estimate.
3. **IGS Product Synchronization:** The International GNSS Service (IGS) precise satellite orbit and clock corrections used by IBGE PPP are generated natively at **30-second** intervals. 

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    subgraph Raw High-Rate Log
        A["1 Hz / 5 Hz Field Log<br/>72,000 Epochs (250 MB)"]
    end

    subgraph RTKCONV Decimation
        B["RTKlib RTKCONV Filter<br/>Time Interval = 30 s"]
    end

    subgraph Geodetic Upload File
        C["30-Second Static RINEX<br/>480 Epochs (1.5 MB)<br/>Zero Loss in Geodetic Accuracy"]
    end

    A --> B --> C
```

Decimating the file to 30 seconds reduces file size by **97%** with **zero loss in final geodetic accuracy**.

---

## Installing RTKLIB for Windows

**RTKLIB** is the industry-standard open-source GNSS analysis suite created by Dr. Tomoji Takasu.

1. Download the latest official Windows release package of RTKLIB (e.g., RTKLIB v2.4.3 or the optimized demo5 fork by Tim Everett) from GitHub:  
   [https://github.com/rtklibexplorer/RTKLIB/releases](https://github.com/rtklibexplorer/RTKLIB/releases) or [http://www.rtklib.com/](http://www.rtklib.com/)
2. Extract the downloaded `.zip` folder to a stable location on your computer (e.g., `C:\Tools\RTKLIB\`).
3. Open the `bin\` subfolder. You will see several graphical tools:
   * `rtkconv.exe`: Format conversion and decimation utility (our primary focus).
   * `rtkpost.exe`: Post-processing kinematic/static baseline solver.
   * `rtkplot.exe`: Residuals, skyplot, and trajectory visualizer.
   * `convbin.exe`: Command-line version of RTKCONV.

---

## Step-by-Step Walkthrough: RTKCONV GUI

Double-click `rtkconv.exe` to launch the conversion window.

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| RTKCONV - RINEX Converter                                       [_][X] |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Time Start (GPST) [x] 2026/03/16 12:00:00  End [x] 2026/03/16 16:00:00 |
| Time Interval     [x] 30 s                 Unit Period      24 h       |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Log File          [ C:\FieldData\ReachRS2_raw_survey.UBX             ] [...] |
| Format            [ Auto / u-blox                                    ] |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Output Directory  [ C:\FieldData\Processed\                          ] [...] |
| RINEX OBS         [ rover_30s.26o                                    ] |
| RINEX NAV         [ rover_30s.26n                                    ] |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| [ Options... ]                                     [ Convert ] [ Exit ] |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### Step 1: Selecting the Input File and Format

1. In the **Log File** field, click the browse button (`...`) and select your raw Emlid Reach RS2 log.
   * If you downloaded the raw log directly from the Emlid receiver via Wi-Fi or Emlid Flow, it is typically named `raw_YYYYMMDDHHMM.UBX`.
   * If you previously exported a RINEX file from Emlid Studio at 1 Hz, select the `.obs` or `.26o` file.
2. In the **Format** dropdown:
   * Select `Auto` or `u-blox` if converting a raw `.UBX` file.
   * Select `RINEX` if decimating an existing high-rate RINEX observation file.

### Step 2: Defining Output File Paths

1. In the **Output Directory** field, choose your clean project destination folder.
2. RTKCONV automatically suggests filenames for the generated RINEX Observation (`.obs` or `.yyO`) and Navigation (`.nav` or `.yyN`) files.

---

### Step 3: Configuring Decimation and RINEX Options

Click the **Options...** button. This opens the configuration window:

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Options                                                          [_][X] |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| RINEX Version   (o) 2.11     ( ) 3.02     ( ) 3.04                     |
| RINEX File Type [x] Observation   [x] Navigation  [ ] GNAV  [ ] HNAV   |
| Frequencies     [x] L1+L2    [x] L5                                    |
| Satellite Syst  [x] GPS      [x] GLONASS  [x] Galileo  [x] BeiDou      |
| Observation Typ [x] C (Pseudorange)  [x] L (Carrier Phase)  [x] D  [x] S|
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Station / Receiver / Antenna Information:                               |
| Marker Name     [ BASE001         ]  Marker Number [ 0001             ] |
| Observer / Agency [ RESEARCHER    ]  [ ECOLOGY LAB                    ] |
| Rec Type/Vers   [ EMLID REACH RS2 ]  [ 3.0                            ] |
| Ant Type/Vers   [ ADVNULLANTENNA  ]  [ NONE                           ] |
| Ant Delta (H/E/N) [ 2.0000 ] m       [ 0.0000 ] m       [ 0.0000 ] m   |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                     [  OK  ] [ Cancel ] |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

Configure each setting carefully:

1. **RINEX Version:**
   * Select **`2.11`**. 
   * *Why:* While RINEX 3.04 supports newer constellation signals, IBGE PPP has historical optimizations for RINEX 2.11 dual-frequency files (GPS L1/L2 + GLONASS G1/G2). RINEX 2.11 guarantees seamless parsing without header syntax rejections.
2. **Time Interval (The Decimation Setting):**
   * Return to the main window (or options dialog depending on RTKLIB build).
   * Check the **Time Interval** box and enter **`30 s`** (or `30.0`).
   * This instructs RTKCONV to extract only epochs matching seconds `:00` and `:30`, discarding the other 29 epochs per 30-second cycle.
3. **Time Start and End Trimming (Optional but Recommended):**
   * Check **Time Start** and **Time End** if you need to crop the file.
   * *Field Tip:* Tripods often wobble slightly while being placed and leveled during the first 2–5 minutes of a survey, and are disturbed when dismantling the station at the end. Trimming the first 5 minutes and last 5 minutes eliminates contaminated carrier-phase observations.
4. **Antenna and Marker Metadata:**
   * **Marker Name:** Enter a 4-to-8 character name identifying your survey benchmark (e.g., `BASE01`).
   * **Antenna Type:** Enter `ADVNULLANTENNA NONE` or `EML_REACH_RS2 NONE`.
   * **Antenna Delta (H/E/N):** Enter the measured vertical height of the tripod or pole in meters (e.g., `2.0000` m) in the **H** box. Leave East and North as `0.0000`.
5. Click **OK** to save options.

---

### Step 4: Executing Conversion

1. On the main window, click **Convert**.
2. The status bar displays processing progress.
3. Upon completion, navigate to your output folder. Notice the difference:
   * Original `.UBX` file: `48,250 KB`
   * Decimated `.26o` file: `1,240 KB`

---

## Verifying the Decimated File Header

Open the generated `.26o` or `.obs` file in Notepad++ or VS Code. Check the ASCII header:

```
     2.11           OBSERVATION DATA    G (GPS)             RINEX VERSION / TYPE
RTKCONV 2.4.3                           20260316 173000 UTC PGM / RUN BY / DATE
BASE01                                                      MARKER NAME
RESEARCHER          ECOLOGY LAB                             OBSERVER / AGENCY
000000              EMLID REACH RS2     3.0                 REC # / TYPE / VERS
000000              ADVNULLANTENNA      NONE                ANT # / TYPE
  3165420.0000 -5523190.0000  -342890.0000                  APPROX POSITION XYZ
        2.0000        0.0000        0.0000                  ANTENNA: DELTA H/E/N
     1     1                                                WAVELENGTH FACT L1/2
     4    L1    L2    C1    P2                              # / TYPES OF OBSERV
   30.000                                                   INTERVAL
  2026     3    16    12     5    0.0000000     GPS         TIME OF FIRST OBS
  2026     3    16    15    55    0.0000000     GPS         TIME OF LAST OBS
                                                            END OF HEADER
```

Look specifically for the **`INTERVAL`** line: it must read **`30.000`**. You now have a compliant RINEX observation file ready for IBGE PPP.

## Command-Line Alternative: `convbin`

If you prefer scripting your workflow or need to batch process multiple survey days, use the command-line utility `convbin.exe` (located in the same `bin\` folder).

Open PowerShell 7 and run:

```powershell
# Convert raw u-blox file to 30-second decimated RINEX 2.11
.\convbin.exe -r ubx -v 2.11 -ti 30 -od -os -o rover_30s.26o -n rover_30s.26n .\raw_reach_rs2.ubx
```

### Explanation of Command-Line Flags

* `-r ubx`: Specifies the input format as u-blox binary.
* `-v 2.11`: Enforces RINEX Version 2.11.
* `-ti 30`: Sets the decimation time interval to 30 seconds.
* `-od`: Includes Doppler frequency measurements in the observation table.
* `-os`: Includes Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) signal strength measurements.
* `-o <filename>`: Specifies the output observation file path.
* `-n <filename>`: Specifies the output broadcast navigation file path.
